key_insight: K/Rb-based lead-free double perovskites beta2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be thermodynamically stable, ductile, and highly tunable in bandgap and thermoelectric performance across Cl/Br/I compositions.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a non-toxic perovskite platform for solar absorbers, tandem/near-IR optoelectronics, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery devices.
method: Density functional theory was used to study structure, mechanics, electronics, optics, and thermoelectrics.
Formation energies, tolerance factors, and octahedral factors were computed to assess stability and cubic phase suitability.
Elastic constants, band structures, and transport-related metrics were analyzed to evaluate ductility, bandgap tuning, and ZT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV and a peak thermoelectric performance of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: Results are theoretical DFT predictions, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, defect tolerance, and device-level performance still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
